reason: Re-opened packet.js veda 6 --verse 1.50.10: Sāyaṇa takes तमसस्परि as above the night (रात्रेरूर्ध्वं) or above darkness that is sin (तमसः पापात् … वा, पापरहितम्), then supports ‘we have come to the highest light’ with the Taittirīya text that he goes to union with the Āditya (आदित्यस्यैव सायुज्यं गच्छति) and endorses it himself (युक्तं चैतत्) by another scripture, as they worship him so they become (तं यथा यथोपासते तदेव भवन्ति). Night-or-sin, union with the Sun, and the become-what-they-worship reason are all in his words; he adopts the quoted texts as his own reading, so attribution holds. Wilson’s ‘supreme spirit’ gloss is not used. Plain sense: 1.50.11 onward is the healing prayer (Sāyaṇa too calls the last tṛca rogaghna), so ‘just before a prayer for healing’ is the text’s own order; no four words of the key repeated. verse.js ok (Rig Veda 1.50.10, at [49,10]); entry-check ok; API confirms revision 401983 is hymn 1.50, 2024-04-24. One softness: Sāyaṇa reads अगन्म as a prayer (may we reach) where Griffith has ‘we have come’, but ‘the coming as union’ does not misstate that. Attacks tried on all nine lines; none lands.
